slides.title: YOLO Quantization
slides.subtitle: YOLO opts: cut post · less compute · better on board
slides.notes: Chapter 2 Model Zoo, lesson 4: YOLO quantization. Last lesson we finished a full ResNet PTQ. This lesson moves to detection—how to cut the heads, where post-process lives, and how to raise sensitive layers. The toolchain adds YOLO-specific opts: cut post-process from the graph, decode on the board, and tune sensitive layers—cutting compute so detection runs better on the board. About fifteen minutes: a clear route, and commands you can follow.

slides.title: Lesson Route
slides.heading: This lesson: ==four questions==
slides.lead: YOLO-specific opts → less compute → better on board.

cards.title: Triage
cards.text: model_info + main; triage by drop size.

slides.notes: Four questions. The toolchain adds YOLO-specific opts—cut post-process, decode on board, raise sensitive layers—so compute drops and detection runs better on the board. First, output heads: classification is one logits path; detection is three strides, each with cls and DFL. Second, cut and decode: export drops post-process; the board restores it with decode_dfl. Third, mapper and sensitive layers: one command into the toolchain; Softmax needs its own setting; raise int16 if still short. Fourth, on-board verify—if accuracy drops, triage before you touch knobs.

items.title: YOLO26
items.text: direct-LTRB: three cls + three 4-channel boxes; separate exporter.

items.title: How to tell
items.text: Read export notes and runtime bindings—do not count output tensors alone.

items.title: Task extensions
items.text: Seg adds mask coeffs/prototypes; pose adds keypoints; classify Softmax stays in runtime.

slides.notes: DFL-family and YOLO26 protocols differ; artifacts are not interchangeable. Compatibility follows export notes and runtime bindings—do not guess from tensor count. Seg, pose, and classify extend the detect protocol.
